name: Context-Gated Threat Response Circuit
short_description: Gates threat responses based on contextual safety cues and prior experience, allowing flexible threat regulation across situations and preventing overgeneralization.

components.name: CONTEXT_GATE
components.description: Opens or closes threat response based on contextual safety cues and learned associations

components.name: PRIOR_EXPERIENCE_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Integrates learned threat history in similar contexts

components.name: RESPONSE_MODULATOR
components.description: Modulates threat response magnitude based on context gate and experience

key_references: Maren, S., Phan, K. L., & Liberzon, I. (2013). The contextual brain: Implications for fear conditioning, extinction and psychopathology. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 14(6), 417–428.
Bouton, M. E. (2004). Context and behavioral processes in extinction. Learning and Memory, 11(5), 485–494.
design_implications: Context-specific threat learning prevents generalized anxiety; design threat-reduction spaces with distinctive contextual markers (visual, acoustic) so safety associations are learned specifically to that context
Extinction learning requires safe re-exposure in context; therapeutic or anxiety-reducing environments should use consistent cues and repeated safe contact to update threat associations
